regime.label: Hawkish hold meets an oil-shock war
regime.oneLiner: June CPI resolved soft (disinflation), but an escalating US-Iran war spiked oil and re-armed the Fed's hike tail — so metals and long-duration stay pressured while energy and defensives lead, and an AI-capex unwind rotates money out of semis into cyclicals; the 28-29 July FOMC (market ~85% hold, live hike tail, no SEP) is the next binary.

topNews.headline: Silver stuck at 8-month lows (~$55.6) as the oil shock lifts rate-hike fears over the safe-haven bid
topNews.actionable: The book's highest-beta pain point — keep leverage sized so the break to 8-month lows can't force liquidation, and let the oil-inflation impulse and the 28-29 July FOMC clear before any deep-value re-entry ($58-60 is the level to reclaim).

topNews.headline: Gold holds the $4,000 shelf (~$4,020) as the PBoC buys a 20th straight month
topNews.actionable: Central-bank demand is a genuine floor near ~$4,000 for the GDX/miner sleeve, but don't expect gold to rescue silver — both hinge on the oil-inflation impulse and the July FOMC; sub-$4,000 is where cash could begin scaling into miners.

topNews.headline: US-Iran war keeps oil bid (WTI ~$82, Brent ~$88); energy is the leading S&P sector
topNews.actionable: The war premium lifts energy but is precisely what's crushing the metals book and pressuring SGX REITs — do NOT add levered silver on the spike; a Hormuz ceasefire is the fast-reversal risk both ways (and would flip metals bullish).

topNews.headline: STI at a record ~5,561; DBS first SGX stock past S$200bn; HK-tech AI-app rotation runs
topNews.actionable: SGX + HK-tech are the book's bright spot; with SG banks extended ~2.2x book into ~6 Aug results, favor SG-centric/data-centre S-REITs on lower-SORA relief and hold Tencent on its buyback bid.

topNews.headline: Lynas CEO Lacaze steps down (interim Le Roux); MP posts record Q1 (+49% revenue)
topNews.actionable: Favor MP (record Q1, DoD $110/kg floor) over Lynas within the cash-funded rare-earth watchlist until Lynas names a permanent CEO; China's export-curb enforcement keeps the ex-China supply thesis intact.
